prize_parts.citation: For the conception and construction of the IceCube neutrino telescope and the discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, opening neutrino astronomy

statement.case_for: IceCube is a discovery in the sense the prize was written for: nature supplied the answer, not a prediction. The 2013 diffuse flux, the 2017-2018 association of a neutrino with the flaring blazar TXS 0506+056, and the Galactic-plane evidence together opened neutrino astronomy as an observational discipline. The enabling step was a kilometre-scale instrumented ice volume, a decades-long detector achievement, and the attribution is comparatively clean: Halzen drove AMANDA and IceCube, and Spiering is a long-standing pioneer of the field. A two-person prize leaves headroom and avoids the leadership-by-proxy problem that arises when a collaboration of thousands must be reduced to three names. The result is mature enough to stand, being independently supported across detection channels, and the discovery is explainable to a general audience as a new window on the Universe.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is credit and completeness. Neutrino-telescope pioneers beyond the credited names (the Baikal collaboration, DUMAND, ANTARES) are not covered, and a two-name prize built on a very large collaboration will be contested. Source identification is only partial: TXS 0506+056 is a single compelling association, and the population origin of the diffuse flux remains open, so the field is still maturing. Finally, only two of the eight members ranked B029 at all (Danielsson and I), so it has a narrower opening base than the clocks; a configuration with broad support such as optical lattice clocks is more likely to survive a full committee vote.

responses.point: Danielsson ranks the Higgs experimental discovery (B026) first and IceCube (B029) second, endorsing a two-person IceCube prize while stressing that the source identification is still partial and that Baikal and DUMAND pioneers complicate credit.
responses.response: I agree on the maturity assessment and take the Baikal and DUMAND point seriously; it is the main reason I would not stretch the IceCube prize to three names. Where I part company is the Higgs ranking. The 2013 prize already honoured the discovery of the mechanism, and the founding-spokesperson trio is a leadership proxy for thousands of people. I rank B026 below IceCube because the attribution there is organisational rather than scientific, although I would accept it as a fall-back if the committee prefers a particle-physics prize this year.

responses.point: Kroll places optical lattice clocks (B042) first, arguing that Katori's magic-wavelength idea is a clean concept, that two laureates is a natural attribution, and that many independent groups confirm 1e-18 uncertainty with a redefinition of the second pending.
responses.response: This is the most persuasive competing case, and four colleagues share it, so I cannot dismiss it as an outlier. The attribution is cleaner than mine and the maturity is excellent. My reservation is that the clocks are a refinement of a measurement capability that earlier prizes (the frequency comb in 2005 and ion control in 2012) largely created, whereas IceCube opens a genuinely new observational channel. That is a judgement about discovery character, not about the quality of the work. I would be comfortable with B042 as the prize and have listed it as my first alternative.

responses.point: Lindroth ranks the clocks first and the Higgs experimental discovery (B026) second, but calls the three-name basis for B026 a leadership-based attribution and is unsure the committee would accept it.
responses.response: I share that hesitation about B026 and it is why I place it third among my own choices. Neither of us has a way to resolve it from the supplied evidence: ATLAS and CMS analysis contributions are diffuse, and honouring spokespersons is not the same as identifying who made the discovery. I would ask whether the committee can articulate a defensible principle before it endorses B026, rather than adopting the trio by default because it is the only available shape.

responses.point: Eriksson ranks tunnel magnetoresistance (B037) first and magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (B054) second, calling the latter an unusually tight link between theory and experiment but acknowledging that the recognition may be somewhat early.
responses.response: The tight theory-to-experiment link in B054 is real and I ranked it sixth for that reason. My concern is timing: the origin of the superconductivity is still debated and the experimental lead author, Yuan Cao, is outside the credited names, so a prize now would crystallise an attribution that the field itself has not settled. I would ask what evidence would convince you the interpretation is stable enough, since waiting a few years costs little.

uncertainties: Whether the committee would accept a two-name IceCube prize given the Baikal, DUMAND and ANTARES pioneers and the size of the IceCube Collaboration.
Whether the population origin of the diffuse neutrino flux is settled enough that the discovery should be treated as complete rather than ongoing.
Whether the committee prefers the broad opening support for optical lattice clocks over the narrower but, in my view, more novel IceCube case.
I am relying on memory of the literature rather than on verified sources for the details of the TXS 0506+056 and Galactic-plane results.
statement.conflict_note: Possible connection to flag: my profile records co-authorship of the Fermi Large Area Telescope instrument paper and membership of gamma-ray and cosmic-ray collaborations (PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGO+), and Fermi-LAT gamma-ray observations were part of the multi-messenger follow-up of the TXS 0506+056 neutrino alert. This is a field-adjacent, collaboration-level link rather than a personal tie to Halzen or Spiering, and I note it so the committee can decide whether recusal is warranted. No specific personal or institutional connection to any other shortlisted candidate is apparent from the provided profile.
